name: Meridian Coffee Roasters

do: Talk about the farmers and the roast, not just the flavour notes
Name origins, roast timing and bag sizes plainly, as facts
Write in the first person plural, as the people who did the roasting
Say what something does not include when it does not include it
dont: Never use wine-tasting jargon: no 'notes of', 'mouthfeel', 'terroir', 'bright acidity', 'finish'
Never claim a health benefit of any kind
Never call the coffee artisanal, craft, premium, curated or hand-crafted
Never call anything revolutionary, game-changing or best-in-class
Never use the word 'journey' about coffee, farmers or customers
Never name or insult a competitor
Never promise anything the offering does not include

offerings.name: Roaster's Choice Subscription
offerings.description: A rotating 340g bag of our current favourite single-origin, roasted fresh and delivered every four weeks.

offerings.name: Origins Gift Box
offerings.description: A one-time gift box with three 200g bags from three different origins, plus a tasting card.

positioning: For people who actually drink their coffee before it dies, Meridian roasts single-origin beans to order in small batches and ships within 48 hours — because the bag on the supermarket shelf was fine once too, several months ago.

composition_plan.intent: First row of the split: the label column names what this business is, the wide column carries the freshness promise and one action, beside a single flat visual field. Not centred, not a full-width band.
The staleness problem set large against a narrow column of detail on how roasting to order answers it. The page's argument, placed before anything is sold.
Order to doorstep as sequential steps, one line of explanation each, so the promise reads as a process someone runs rather than a slogan. The list supplies the numbering.
A ruled band of the given figures, each under a short label, so the freshness claim is legible as data at a glance.
The catalogue side by side, one column per offering, each showing what is included and what is not, so a visitor can choose without reading prose.
One full-width row per point of difference — sourcing, batch size, roast-to-ship discipline — one idea to a row, no cards.
Absorb the practical friction — skipping, cancelling, what falls outside each offering — so the catalogue section stays clean.
Ground the roastery in a real street, phone and inbox. Nothing else in this section.
